clue.text: Sleep with dandy in car on the way back

indicators.note: the whole assembled car-with-dandy is read in the return direction
the dandy sits inside the car's name

parts.note: the Ford is a make of car
a fop is a man too concerned with his clothes

explanation.surface: Someone dozes beside a dapper companion while being driven home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is the everyday phrasal verb for falling asleep.

clue.text: All the other instruments I rope in to play

indicators.note: the letters are set to play, loosely rearranged like a performance

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician wants to enlist the rest of the orchestra for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripieno is the full orchestral body in a Baroque concerto grosso, as opposed to the soloists.
explanation.definitionFit: In a concerto grosso the ripieno is the main ensemble playing alongside the small solo group.

clue.text: Brief: mine handy?

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
read as 'h and y', the two letters joined

explanation.surface: A curt query about whether a mine is conveniently close.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is splitting 'handy' into 'h and y': just those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy remark is concise and to the point, a synonym of brief.

clue.text: Spur cut around American pasta

indicators.note: the shortened spur goes about the abbreviation for American
the stimulus word loses its final letter, docked short

parts.note: a fillip is a stimulus or spur

explanation.surface: A cowboy's spur trimmed beside some American pasta, a culinary oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusilli are spiral-shaped pasta shapes, a kind of Italian noodle.

clue.text: Van finally removed from house on street, space reserved

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade 'on' puts the house after the street
one letter is taken out of the house's name

parts.note: the House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word van is meant

parts.note: the last letter of van

explanation.surface: A removal van leaves a house, and space is kept free on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' here means a royal dynasty, not a building: the House of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is room set aside for keeping things, space kept for later use.

clue.text: Posh, cute dandy?

parts.note: twee is cute in an over-sweet way
read as 'd and y', the two letters joined

explanation.surface: A description of someone stylish: upper-class, sweet, a bit of a fop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' is split as 'd and y', the same trick as in other clues here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy describes the country-gentry style of the upper classes, hence refined and well-to-do.

clue.text: Storyteller, creator uninvolved?

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
split as UN plus 'involved': UN joins the letters to be mixed, and 'involved', meaning tangled, signals the mixing

explanation.surface: Asks whether a storyteller is a creator who stays detached from the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'uninvolved' into UN plus 'involved': UN joins the fodder and 'involved' signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person skilled at telling anecdotes, a teller of tales.

clue.text: Time off from study, stuff inspiring a playboy on vacation

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the stuff takes the other letters inside

parts.note: gear is kit, stuff
taken as written

indicators.note: the playboy is vacated, emptied of everything but his outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of playboy, once emptied

explanation.surface: A playboy on holiday is motivated by his kit while taking a break from college.
explanation.walkthrough: A gap year is the British name for a year out, usually between school and university.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is a twelve-month break taken before or during higher education.

clue.text: Ace — another card, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a different card is, literally, some other thing

explanation.surface: A card player hesitates between an ace and a different card.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is an example: any card other than the one in question is just another thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is colloquial praise for something outstanding and also literally means a different item.

clue.text: Rotation of valved devices in row

indicators.note: rotating turns the devices' name end to end

parts.note: taps control flow with a valve

explanation.surface: A plumber turning valves in a line of fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, and a row is an argument.

clue.text: With these, washers' heads in coverings of plastic spattered?

definitions.text: With these, washers' heads in coverings of plastic spattered?

indicators.note: spattered means splashed about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the three words is taken

parts.note: the heads of these three words supply three letters

explanation.surface: People washing keep their hair in plastic covers while being splashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also gives the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shower caps are waterproof plastic hats bathers wear to keep their hair dry.

clue.text: Doctor who transformed state in setter, briefly

indicators.note: the state goes inside the shortened setter
the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: jelly is something that sets
KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A shape-shifting doctor puts a US state inside the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, but means jelly, which sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll, in Stevenson's tale, changes into the monstrous Mr Hyde.

clue.text: Put in peril, give peace a chance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to expose to danger
second meaning, read cryptically as the answer: stop being angry

explanation.surface: Endangering something versus the hippie slogan about peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 3,5 to see the second sense: ending anger is a step towards peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to risk or harm.

clue.text: Function with metrical swinging of wood chopper, did you say?

indicators.note: asks whether a phrase was spoken, so the letters come from pronunciation

parts.note: a logger fells trees, and his metrical swinging is his rhythm: 'logger rhythm'

explanation.surface: A mathematician hears the beat of an axeman at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Logger rhythm' read out loud gives the mathematical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is a mathematical function, the inverse of exponentiation.

clue.text: Injected substance ruins meat that's processed

indicators.note: processed food is altered, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something injected into meat spoils it when processed.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is blood serum containing antibodies, given by injection for immunity.

clue.text: Inebriated worker randy?

parts.note: the worker bee is the standard crossword worker
read as 'r and y', the two letters joined

explanation.surface: A drunk employee who is feeling lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Randy' is split as 'r and y'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beery means affected by beer drinking, tipsy or drunk.

clue.text: Moderate taking a badger by the ear?

indicators.note: judging by the ear means going by sound

parts.note: to bait is to badger or harass, so 'a badger' is 'a bait'

explanation.surface: Someone restrained grabbing a badger's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal, but is the verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or die down, to become moderate.

clue.text: Cheese sandwiches first of all on order, choose ham roll

indicators.note: the cheese surrounds the other letters, as bread does a filling

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A deli order: cheese sandwiches, then a ham roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' is the definition, not part of the food order.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, enriched French bread bun.

clue.text: Wind and frost unfortunately resulted in winter pile-up?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad weather caused a multi-car crash on an icy road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile-up' looks like a crash but means a heap of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowdrift is a bank of snow heaped up by the wind in cold weather.

clue.text: Going to that place, put on number for the audience?

indicators.note: what an audience gets is the sound, not the spelling

parts.note: to wear is to put on, and two is a number: 'wear two'

explanation.surface: A performer asks where to go, then dons the second outfit for the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereto is an old adverb meaning towards which place.

clue.text: Eggs having gone up in smoke, Shrove Tuesday over, evidently?

indicators.note: the eggs end up inside the smoke

parts.note: a fag is British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice

explanation.surface: Pancake eggs burnt to smoke once Pancake Day is past.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday precedes Lent, the Christian season of abstinence, so its end means going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent, starting the day after Shrove Tuesday, is traditionally a time of abstaining from food.

clue.text: Plate with lamb or chicken, perhaps, served up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: both are examples of an animal

explanation.surface: A dinner plate bearing lamb or chicken, brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' looks like crockery but is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or plate of material, as of bone or metal.

clue.text: Distort the winning beauty of modern art?

parts.note: a beauty pageant winner is titled Miss
Tate Modern is London's modern art gallery

explanation.surface: A critic warps the image of a pageant winner in a contemporary artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate is to report wrongly, to misrepresent the facts.

clue.text: A blind partner's exploit in rave

parts.note: in the British phrase 'eff and blind', meaning to swear, eff pairs with blind
to use is to exploit

explanation.surface: A sightless person's companion takes advantage at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' is not about sight: 'to eff and blind' is a British idiom for swearing profusely.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out words gushingly, to gush or enthuse.

clue.text: Crave cool candy?

parts.note: a fan cools you down
read as 'c and y', the two letters joined

explanation.surface: Wanting some chilled sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candy' is split as 'c and y'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to want or desire it.

clue.text: Evidence of damage, problem with electrical connection?

parts.note: SCART is the 21-pin plug once used to link TVs and video equipment
an issue is a problem

explanation.surface: A technician finds damage caused by a faulty wiring link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scar tissue is the fibrous tissue that forms where a wound has healed, showing past injury.

clue.text: Green piece of lasagna I found

indicators.note: only a piece of the run of letters is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of lasagna, the I and the start of found

explanation.surface: A diner finds a green bit in the lasagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' means inexperienced, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif means naive, innocent or unworldly, like someone green.

clue.text: Man ripe for development in geologic period

indicators.note: development changes form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fully grown man ready for evolution across geological time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Permian is the last era of the Palaeozoic, roughly 299 to 252 million years ago.

clue.text: Toy with a hog that's furious in sweaty exercise

indicators.note: fury suggests wild agitation, so the letters are tossed about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry pig being played with during a sweaty workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot yoga is yoga practised in a heated room, a strenuous sweaty workout.
